title: Double tops and double bottoms
desc: Two failed tries at a level, and why only the break confirms it

cards.title: Second try at $100
cards.situation: A stock rose to $100, fell to $90, rose to $100 again and failed. Now it’s at $95. Is the double top confirmed?

chart.label: Two peaks at $100 with a $90 middle low; price now $95

options.text: Yes: two peaks at $100 is enough
options.feedback: Two peaks show sellers defending $100. The pattern only counts when price breaks the middle low.

options.text: Not yet: it needs to close below $90
options.feedback: Until $90 breaks, it’s a range between $90 and $100, not a confirmed top.

options.text: Yes: any drop from the second peak counts
options.feedback: A drop from the second peak is normal inside a range. The top counts only on a close below the $90 middle low.

cards.work: Peaks $100 and $100. Middle low $90. Now $95: still above $90.

cards.title: Two failed attempts
cards.text: When price tries a level twice and fails twice, the side that failed may be running out of steam. The point between the two tries is the **middle**.

items.label: Double top
items.sub: Two tries at a high. Buyers failed twice.

items.label: Double bottom
items.sub: Two tries at a low. Sellers failed twice.

blocks.tip: Confirmation is a close through the middle point. Until then, it’s just a range.

cards.title: Confirm, then measure
cards.text: A [[double-bottom|double bottom]] at $50 with a middle high at $56. A close above $56 confirms it.

chart.label: A double bottom at $50 breaks above the $56 middle; the rough target is $62

cards.foot: A rough guide: the height of the pattern added to the break. $56 − $50 = $6, so about $62. A guide, never a promise.

cards.title: Two peaks, sure fall?
cards.myth: Two peaks at the same price always mean a fall.

visual.title: Never confirmed
visual.label: Two peaks at the same price, but price never closes below the middle low and climbs above the peaks

cards.reality: Many [[double-top|double tops]] never break the middle low. Some keep ranging. Some break out above the peaks.
cards.added: Board P1-Ch04-L4 card 4: the “Never confirmed” chart

cards.title: Find the trigger
cards.q: A double bottom: lows at $30 and $30.50, with a middle high at $34. Where is it confirmed?

chart.label: Lows at $30 and $30.50 with a middle high at $34

options.feedback: At the second low, nothing has been proven yet. The close above the $34 middle high confirms it.
The close above the $34 middle high shows sellers failed twice. Until then, it’s a range.
A close below $30 breaks both lows. That cancels the double bottom instead of confirming it.
Halfway up proves nothing. The pattern counts only on a close above the $34 middle high.

cards.title: A rough target
cards.q: A double top: peaks at $80, middle low at $72. Price closes below $72. Where is a rough first target?

options.feedback: The pattern is $8 tall. Take that from the $72 break: about $64. A guide, never a promise.
$72 is where the pattern triggers. The rough target takes the pattern’s height away from that break.
$80 is the peak sellers defended. After a break below $72, the rough target sits below the break, not above.
$88 adds the height on top of the peaks. A double top points down: take the height away from the $72 break.

cards.headline: You can spot a failed attempt.
lines: Double top: two failed tries at a high. Double bottom: at a low.
It’s confirmed only on a close through the middle point.
